src_text: As the threshold model {{PT_CITE_1}} can generate perfectly nested networks for different choices of the fitness distribution {{PT_CITE_2}}, one might wonder whether it would be possible to generate perfectly nested networks with arbitrary network topology.{{NL}}Hagberg et al. {{PT_CITE_3}} provided a recipe to do that, approximately, for large enough networks.{{NL}}To this end, they introduced a creation-sequence mechanism for the generation of a threshold network, i.e., a perfectly nested network. The mechanism is simple: before creating the network, one partitions the nodes into the dominant and the independent set (see Section {{PT_REF_4}}). At each time step, a new node is added to the network. If the newcomer is a dominant node, it connects to all the preexisting nodes. If the newcomer is an independent node, it remains isolated. It is evident that this growth mechanism generates a perfectly nested structure.{{NL}}Therefore, if we define a node-level binary variable {{PT_MATH_5}} which is equal to one and zero for dominant and independent nodes, respectively, the growth of the perfectly nested network can be encoded in a creation sequence {{PT_MATH_6}}. src_text: The RIR generator is based on the ISM and considers two cases: shoe box, i.e.{{NL}}rectangular, and arbitrary polyhedral rooms. For shoe box rooms, the original{{NL}}algorithm from Allen and Berkley {{PT_CITE_1}} is used. In this case,{{NL}}symmetries limit the number of image sources to grow quadratically and{{NL}}cubically in 2D and 3D, respectively, in the order of reflections. In addition,{{NL}}image sources are always visible from anywhere in the room. The situation for{{NL}}arbitrary polyhedral rooms is not that simple. The number of image sources grows{{NL}}exponentially in the order of reflections and the visibility of{{NL}}sources must be checked. When obtuse angles occur between walls, the{{NL}}reflections from these walls will not be visible in the whole room. In{{NL}}addition, if the room is not convex, i.e. re-entrant walls occur, they{{NL}}might obstruct the path between image sources and microphones. Both situations{{NL}}are illustrated in Figure {{PT_REF_2}}. The algorithm is explained in detail in the original{{NL}}paper by Borish {{PT_CITE_3}}. In practice, we found its pure Python{{NL}}implementation to be too slow to be practical and hence moved to compiled C code{{NL}}for that part of the package.
tgt_text: RIR生成器基于ISM，并考虑两种情况：鞋盒式（即矩形）房间和任意多面体房间。对于鞋盒式房间，使用Allen and Berkley {{PT_CITE_1}}的原始算法。在这种情况下，{{NL}}对称性使得镜像源的数量随反射阶数在2D和3D中分别呈二次和三次增长。此外，{{NL}}镜像源在房间内任何位置都始终可见。对于{{NL}}任意多面体房间，情况则不那么简单。镜像源的数量随反射阶数呈{{NL}}指数增长，并且必须检查声源的{{NL}}可见性。当墙面之间存在钝角时，{{NL}}来自这些墙面的反射不会在整个房间内可见。{{NL}}此外，如果房间不是凸的，即存在凹入墙，它们{{NL}}可能会遮挡镜像源与麦克风之间的路径。这两种情况{{NL}}在图{{PT_REF_2}}中均有说明。该算法在Borish {{PT_CITE_3}}的原始论文中有详细解释。在实践中，我们发现其纯Python{{NL}}实现速度太慢，不实用，因此将该部分功能移至编译的C代码中{{NL}}。

src_text: In Learning to Think {{PT_CITE_1}}, it is acceptable that the RNN M is not always a reliable predictor. Unlike this early work, however, we use evolution for C (like in Learning to Think) rather than traditional RL combined with RNNs, which has the advantage of both simplicity and generality.

src_text: For the M Model, we use an LSTM {{PT_CITE_1}} recurrent neural network combined with a Mixture Density Network {{PT_CITE_2}} as the output layer. We use this network to model the probability distribution of the next {{PT_MATH_3}} in the next time step as a Mixture of Gaussian distribution. This approach is very similar to {{PT_CITE_4}} in the Unconditional Handwriting Generation section and also the decoder-only section of SketchRNN {{PT_CITE_5}}. The only difference in the approach used is that we did not model the correlation parameter between each element of {{PT_MATH_6}}, and instead had the MDN-RNN output a diagonal covariance matrix of a factored Gaussian distribution.

src_text: Next, starting from the context vector, the decoding process generates the text descriptions. The description of a medical image usually contains multiple sentences, and each sentence focuses on one specific topic. Our model leverages this compositional structure to generate reports in a hierarchical way: it first generates a sequence of high-level topic vectors representing sentences, then generates a sentence from each topic vector. Specifically, the context vector is inputted into a sentence LSTM, which unrolls for a few steps and produces a topic vector at each step. A topic vector represents the semantics of a sentence to be generated. Given a topic vector, the word LSTM takes it as input and generates a sequence of words to form a sentence. The termination of the unrolling process is controlled by the sentence LSTM.

src_text: The evaluation metrics show that both of the algorithms has high precision rate (99.66% for Faster R-CNN vs 99.73% for YOLOv3). Considering F1, which is a harmonic average of the precision and recall that gives a global idea about robustness of the algorithm (his ability to extract all the instances of cars and to not falsely extract non-car objects). We note here that YOLOv3 outperforms Faster R-CNN as it has higher recall. The quality measure is a similar metric to measure the robustness of the algorithm. src_text: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are being more and more adopted in surveillance and monitoring tasks due to their flexibility and great mobility. UAVs produce high resolution images for wide fields of view in real time. The adoption of UAVs have been inhibited first by the low accuracy of object detection algorithms based on the traditional approaches of machine learning. However, since the emergence of deep learning algorithms and especially the convolution neural networks, object detection and recognition have shown a notable increase of accuracy. This paves the way towards a widespread adoption of UAVs for data acquisition and analysis in many engineering fields. This is why it is estimated that UAV global sales are expected to surpass $12 billion by 2021 {{PT_CITE_1}}.

src_text: A complete diagnostic report for a medical image is comprised of both text descriptions (long paragraphs) and lists of tags, as shown in Figure {{PT_REF_1}}. We propose a multi-task hierarchical model with co-attention for automatically predicting keywords and generating long paragraphs. Given an image which is divided into regions, we use a CNN to learn visual features for these patches. Then these visual features are fed into a multi-label classification (MLC) network to predict the relevant tags. In the tag vocabulary, each tag is represented by a word-embedding vector. Given the predicted tags for a specific image, their word-embedding vectors serve as the semantic features of this image. Then the visual features and semantic features are fed into a co-attention model to generate a context vector that simultaneously captures the visual and semantic information of this image. As of now, the encoding process is completed.

src_text: Like early RNN-based C–M systems  {{PT_CITE_1}}, ours simulates possible futures time step by time step, without profiting from human-like hierarchical planning or abstract reasoning, which often ignores irrelevant spatial-temporal details. A systematic analysis of other representative examples of anomalous diffusion,{{NL}}of combinations of different anomalous diffusions, and of processes with dynamical{{NL}}transitions between different types of behavior is thus ultimately necessary, in order{{NL}}to attain a full understanding of the spectral content of a single-trajectory PSD.{{NL}}In turn, such an analysis will provide robust criteria permitting eventually{{NL}}to distinguish between different types of random motion. Our work thus represents an{{NL}}essential first step in this direction.
